sentences.text: Issi saaneq, meaning "cold bone," is the only known species of a plateosaurid dinosaur that lived in Greenland during the Late Triassic period.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a relatively complete skull that is partly articulated, measuring 243.7 millimetres in preserved length.
This individual represents a later-stage juvenile or subadult, offering a glimpse into the development of these ancient reptiles.
Issi holds the distinction of being the first non-avian dinosaur species ever described from Greenland.
A skull of a basal sauropodomorph was uncovered on July 27, 1991, by a Harvard University team led by Farish Jenkins on Jameson Land in northeastern Greenland.

The species Issi saaneq was named and described in 2021 by Victor Beccari Dieguez Campo, Octávio Mateus, Oliver Wings, Jesper Milàn, and Lars Bjørn Clemmensen, who reinterpreted it as a distinct genus that is the sister species of Plateosaurus.
Issi is classified within the family Plateosauridae, which belongs to the broader parent group and class Saurischia.
